headline: Atlanta is a 3.5 road price after 163 rush yards and two giveaways

sectionTitles.currentState: A 6-2 club with a deadline and day-to-day tags
sectionTitles.gamePlan: What the 3.5 number actually asks in Atlanta
sectionTitles.pressConferences: Monday podium after the Jets win

dek: Kansas City is 6-2 and goes to the Atlanta Falcons on Sun Nov 15, 12:00 PM CT on CBS laying 3.5, with a 35-12 win over the Jets still carrying two turnovers onto the trip.
videoHook: Atlanta is the assignment, the number is 3.5, and the last tape is a 35-12 win that still gave the ball away twice.
theEdge: ESPN FPI puts Kansas City at 78.1 percent to win in Atlanta, and DraftKings lists the Chiefs minus 3.5 on a 45.5 total — a road favorite whose 23-of-31, 117.9 line still came with two sacks, eight quarterback hits, and two turnovers.
editorNotes: NYJ made FGs of 23, 48, 49, 54, all before halftime. KC made no field goal. Misses: Sanders 53 wide left, Butker 51 wide right.
Allen fumble: forced by Bolton, recovered by Gilman. Do not credit Bolton as the recoverer.
Mahomes sack count is 2. Geno Smith was sacked five times. Jones leader line is 2 sacks. KC QB hits 7; hits on Mahomes 8.
Briningstool and Canady holdings are not tagged wiped play.
Eligible list: Nourzad on Q1 5:40; Tonga on Q4 3:35. Do not merge those reports.
Three day-to-day names are incomplete in the Pride snippet beyond Mahomes. Butker is a Reid concern in the Addict headline, not a listed status.
No completed trade is in the supplied items. Deadline item dates the cutoff as Tuesday, November 10, 3:00 p.m. Arrowhead time.
Last-game window is midday. Do not use the word night anywhere.

pressConferences.title: Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes, Chris Jones & Ken Walker Postgame Press Conferences - NFL Week 9

storyline.lede: The next kickoff is in Atlanta, Sun Nov 15, 12:00 PM CT on CBS, with Kansas City laying 3.5 on a 45.5 total and ESPN FPI giving the Chiefs a 78.1 percent chance. That price is the story. The 35-12 win over the Jets is the supporting tape: 391 yards, five touchdowns, and two turnovers that a road favorite cannot treat as scenery.
body: Andy Reid, Eric Bieniemy, and Steve Spagnuolo got the get-well version of the offense and the rush they have been waiting to see travel. Patrick Mahomes finished 23-of-31 for 242 yards and two touchdown passes, rating 117.9, with two sacks. The team ran for 163 on 32 attempts and threw for 228 net. Arrowhead Pride’s film look had the running backs at 27 carries for 155 yards and two touchdowns. That is a real identity. It is also a home identity until it shows up on the road.

The Jets still held the ball for 31:06 to Kansas City’s 28:54, posted 106 rushing yards, and kicked their way to 12 points before the half. Kansas City’s two turnovers — Justin Fields’ fumble, recovered by Davis, and a Mahomes fumble forced by Bailey and recovered by McDonald — are the stains on a 27-first-down afternoon. Arrowhead Addict called it the defense Spagnuolo had been waiting to see, and also warned that harder tests are next.

Atlanta is that test on the calendar, then Arizona at Arrowhead on Sun Nov 22, 12:00 PM CT, then Buffalo on Thu Nov 26, 7:20 PM CT. Arrowhead Pride’s Week 10 rankings roundup has ESPN leaving the Chiefs at No. 6. The same outlet’s playoff picture says the 35-12 win kept pace rather than creating separation. Arrowhead Addict notes the Super Bowl 61 price moved the wrong way after the win. A 6-2 record can be both real and unfinished. Brett Veach’s trade-deadline window, with Reid saying Veach keeps his eyes open, is the roster question sitting beside the Atlanta script.

lastGameReview.label: Week 9 · Sun, Nov 8 · 12:00 PM CT
lastGameReview.lede: At Arrowhead, the Jets led 6–0 on field goals of 23 and 48 yards, the second of them at Q1 4:35, before Kansas City scored five touchdowns and won 35-12. New York’s other scores were a 49-yard field goal and a 54-yard field goal, both before halftime. Kansas City did not make a field goal.

analysis.body: The comeback was a drive story, not a trick. Net passing was 228. The rush total was 163 on 32 attempts. Possession sat at 28:54, so the Jets’ 31:06 did not come with control of the sticks. Smith finished 18-of-32 with a 70.4 rating and was sacked five times. Breece Hall had 18 touches and Braelon Allen 10, and the Jets still managed 106 rushing yards on 25 attempts. That is a front that bent and then ended drives.

Emmett Johnson’s 6-yard touchdown at Q4 3:35 came with Tonga reported eligible on that snap. Travis Kelce caught four passes for 72 yards. Rashee Rice had five catches, Xavier Worthy six. Those are the touches Bieniemy can actually pack.

The two giveaways are specific. At Q1 5:40, with Nourzad reported eligible, Fields went up the middle and lost the ball, recovered by Davis. At Q2 1:41, Bailey sacked Mahomes for a 10-yard loss and McDonald recovered. An earlier Bailey sack-fumble was recovered by Moore, so it stayed with Kansas City. Bolton forced Allen’s fumble at Q2 6:29 and Gilman recovered it. That is the Jets’ one turnover. Mahomes was also hit eight times and sacked twice. Kansas City recorded 7 quarterback hits. Harrison Butker missed a 51-yard field goal wide right; Sanders missed from 53, wide left. Jake Briningstool was flagged for offensive holding in the first quarter and J. Canady for offensive holding in the third. Those flags are on the sheet. They are not listed as wiped plays.

After halftime the scoreboard belonged to Kansas City: a 1-yard touchdown at Q3 10:20, Walker’s 2-yard score, and Johnson’s 6-yard score. New York’s late drives ended on downs, including Karlaftis’ sack of Smith at Q4 11:47. The tape says the run game and the red-zone finishes traveled from the second quarter into the fourth. It also says the protection and the ball security did not.

takeaways.title: The run total is a team number
takeaways.body: Kansas City rushed for 163 yards on 32 attempts. Walker’s 102 yards on 18 carries are the lead line inside that total, not a substitute for it. Pride’s backfield split of 27 carries for 155 yards is the same idea from the film desk.

takeaways.title: Two giveaways sit on an otherwise clean count
takeaways.body: The box lists two Kansas City turnovers and one for New York. Davis recovered the Fields fumble. McDonald recovered the Mahomes fumble Bailey forced. Gilman recovered the Allen fumble Bolton forced.

whatWorked: Walker’s 22 touches and a 163-yard team rush that included a 2-yard touchdown up the middle.
Mahomes at 23-of-31, 242 yards, two touchdown passes, rating 117.9, with Kelce at 4 catches for 72 yards.
whatDidnt: Two turnovers, including a sack-fumble Mahomes lost, on a day he was also hit eight times and sacked twice.
Butker’s 51-yard miss wide right, and holding flags on Briningstool and Canady.
Kickoff-return ball security: Stiggers forced a fumble that Bassa recovered, so it did not become a turnover, but it was loose.

currentState.lede: The Chiefs are 6-2, ESPN’s power ranking is unchanged at 6, and the next three kickoffs are Atlanta, Arizona, and Buffalo. The staff’s live questions are ball security, Mahomes’ day-to-day tag, and whether Veach adds a piece before the deadline cutoff Reid’s podium was already discussing.

workOn.title: Protect the second sack
workOn.body: Mahomes was sacked twice and hit eight times. One of those sacks became a fumble McDonald recovered, and the play-by-play notes he was injured on that play. Atlanta will not need a exotic plan if the pocket looks like Q2 1:41.

workOn.title: Finish the possession that starts minus the ball
workOn.body: Fields’ fumble, with Nourzad reported eligible, handed New York the ball at the Kansas City 34. A 6-2 road favorite cannot donate a short field and then rely on five touchdowns to erase it.

workOn.title: Decide the Walker dose before Thursday in Buffalo
workOn.body: Walker already has a 22-touch game on the sheet. Arizona is Sun Nov 22, 12:00 PM CT, and Buffalo is Thu Nov 26, 7:20 PM CT. Bieniemy can feature him in Atlanta without emptying the tank if Johnson (6 touches) and Jaydn Ott (3) stay in the script, the way they did after the game was in hand.

thinkAbout.title: How much of 6-2 is the opponent
thinkAbout.body: Arrowhead Addict argues the record deserves more respect than the critics allow, and also notes Kansas City is not the only club helped by schedule. FPI’s 78.1 percent in Atlanta is a strong number. It is not a certificate.

thinkAbout.title: Whether the deadline is a receiver week
thinkAbout.body: Arrowhead Pride reports smoke at wide receiver and quotes Reid saying Veach keeps his eyes open, with the cutoff described as Tuesday, November 10, at 3:00 p.m. Arrowhead time. Rice, Worthy, and Kelce just produced the catch counts. A deal would change the Atlanta menu. No deal is listed as completed.

thinkAbout.title: What day-to-day means for the starter
thinkAbout.body: Arrowhead Pride says Reid labeled three players day-to-day and names Mahomes in that group. Arrowhead Addict says Reid also addressed concerns about Mahomes, Butker, and mounting injuries. The quarterback finished the Jets game. The tag still belongs in the Atlanta meeting.

gamePlan.lede: Kansas City is a 3.5-point road favorite on Sun Nov 15, 12:00 PM CT on CBS, in a 45.5 total, with FPI at 78.1 percent. The assignment is to take the Jets’ efficient down-and-distance tape on the road without the two giveaways, and to make Spagnuolo’s rush a weekly habit rather than a home spike.
gamePlan.howTheyMatch: Spagnuolo can lean on the 7 quarterback hits and Jones’ two sacks as the standard, not as a prediction of another five-sack day.

keys.title: Live in inside zone before the shot
keys.body: Walker’s up-the-middle carries were the profitable pattern on the Jets tape. In Atlanta, Bieniemy should stay on that downhill look on first down so Mahomes is not asked to create from a muddied pocket.

keys.title: Give Kelce and Rice the third-down rub
keys.body: Kelce’s 72 yards on four catches and Rice’s five receptions are the answers when the rush is closing. Mesh and a sit route beat hero ball on third-and-medium.

keys.title: Rush the sticks, then drop into two-deep
keys.body: The Jets managed 15 first downs and 2-of-12 on third down when the rush arrived. Cover-2 after a simulated pressure is the call that keeps a home underdog from stealing a 54-yard field-goal kind of drive.

keys.title: Treat 22 touches as a plan, not a dare
keys.body: Walker can lead the script. Johnson and Ott are already in the touch list. Saving a few early-down carries matters with Arizona and Buffalo on the next two lines.

script: Open with under-center inside zone to Walker and a Mahomes keep only if the end crashes, the way his two rushes against the Jets stayed small.
On the first third-and-medium, throw mesh to Kelce and Rice with Worthy clearing the corner, and keep Noah Gray as the check if the linebacker walls it.
Boot off the run fake once Atlanta widens to Walker, with Worthy on the perimeter and Kelce in the flat.
Use a Walker screen when the hit count starts to look like the eight from last game, and let the line lead.

In the red zone, condense and hand to Walker up the middle before asking Mahomes for a fourth-down throw. The Jets tape finished with short touchdowns, including Johnson from the 6 with Tonga reported eligible.

Defensively, open in Cover-2 on early downs and call a zone blitz on second-and-long, with Jones occupying and a second-level rusher free. Rally Bolton and the linebackers. Do not spend the takeaway on a blitz story the Jets tape does not need.

spotlight.title: 78.1 percent is still a one-score lean
spotlight.body: DraftKings has Kansas City minus 3.5, not minus 10. FPI’s 78.1 percent is the model’s lean. A 45.5 total says the market does not expect another 35-point Kansas City afternoon by default.

spotlight.title: 102 yards inside a 163-yard team rush
spotlight.body: Walker had 18 carries for 102 yards. Pride’s film review put the backs at 155 yards on 27 carries. That is the Atlanta carry plan.

spotlight.title: Two sacks and a rush that looked like the old standard
spotlight.body: Jones is the sack leader from the Jets game with two. Arrowhead Addict tied the larger day — Smith sacked five times, 7 quarterback hits — to the defense Spagnuolo has wanted, and flagged harder tests ahead. Atlanta is the next one.

spotlight.title: ESPN left them at 6
spotlight.body: Arrowhead Pride’s Week 10 roundup says the national board strengthened a top-10 placement and ESPN did not move the Chiefs off 6. Keeping pace, which the same site’s playoff picture also stressed, is the honest frame.

spotlight.title: Veach’s eyes are open; the roster is not rewritten yet
spotlight.body: Reid’s Monday answer, via Arrowhead Pride, is that Veach keeps his eyes open, with receiver smoke in the same report. Until a move is announced, Rice, Worthy, Jalen Royals, and Kelce are the pass-game names on the touch list.

matchups.unit: Chiefs run game vs. Atlanta’s front
matchups.chiefs: Walker, Johnson, Ott behind Bieniemy’s zone
matchups.opponent: Atlanta’s early-down front, unlisted by player in this packet
matchups.note: The Jets tape is 163 rushing yards on 32 attempts and Walker at 102 on 18. That is the edge Kansas City actually owns until Atlanta proves otherwise.

matchups.unit: Mahomes vs. the rush he just faced
matchups.opponent: A home pass rush that can copy eight hits
matchups.note: The completion line is excellent. Two sacks, eight quarterback hits, and a lost fumble are why the edge is not a clean Kansas City win.
It is not a promise of the same sack total.

matchups.opponent: A Falcons offense that has to stay on schedule at home
matchups.note: New York was 2-of-12 and held a 31:06 possession edge without turning it into points after halftime. Winning third down is how a 3.5 road favorite separates.

matchups.unit: Ball security vs. a short field
matchups.chiefs: Two turnovers, including the Fields fumble Davis recovered
matchups.opponent: Atlanta’s field-position game if it starts inside the 40
matchups.note: Five touchdowns covered the donations against the Jets. A 45.5 road game is less forgiving if McDonald’s recovery has a sequel.

xsandos.title: Walker inside zone on first down
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10 at Atlanta, early, before the pocket gets loud
xsandos.why: Walker just posted 102 yards on 18 carries, and the team rush was 163 on 32. His up-the-middle carries against the Jets, including the 2-yard touchdown, are the downhill picture Bieniemy should replay so Mahomes is not living on eight-hit timing.
xsandos.coaching: Zone steps, one cut, Walker presses the point and bends off the first free hat. Johnson spells him. Mahomes is the keeper only if the end crashes inside.

labels.te: zone combo to the second level

xsandos.title: Mesh for Kelce and Rice
xsandos.situation: 3rd-and-5 to 3rd-and-7 in Atlanta, rush heat showing
xsandos.why: Kelce had four catches for 72 yards and Rice five catches in a 6-of-11 third-down game. Rubs give Mahomes a throw before the hit count from the Jets tape repeats.
xsandos.coaching: Kelce and Rice cross at depth, Worthy runs the corner route, Gray sits if the linebacker runs with the crosser. Mahomes throws the rub, not the hero shot, unless the safety bails.

xsandos.title: Walker screen when the hits stack
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-8 after a pressure look, anywhere on the Atlanta side of midfield
xsandos.why: Mahomes took eight quarterback hits and two sacks, and one sack became a lost fumble. Walker already caught four balls. A screen is the answer that uses his 22-touch role without another dropback into traffic.
xsandos.coaching: Let the line release and lead. Walker catches behind the rush and runs to the numbers. Ott can take the same picture later so Walker is not the screen and the inside zone on every snap.

xsandos.title: Boot off the zone sell
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10 in Atlanta after two inside-zone looks have widened the end
xsandos.why: The run fake is earned by 163 rush yards, not by a Jets throw the play-by-play never labeled as play-action. Moving Mahomes to the perimeter is how Reid and Bieniemy cut the eight-hit problem without abandoning Walker.
xsandos.coaching: Sell inside zone, boot Mahomes to the boundary, Worthy on the out, Kelce leaking flat, Rice on the glance if the safety drives. Throw the easy one. Scramble only if both are covered, the way his two rushes stayed modest against the Jets.

xsandos.title: Cover-2 on Atlanta’s early down
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10, Atlanta in plus territory, no need to chase a big play
xsandos.why: Against the Jets, deep shots to Mitchell were incomplete or wiped by an illegal shift, and the completed explosives did not become a second-half score. Two deep and five under lets Bolton, Tranquill, and Conner rally the way they did on Hall and Allen.
xsandos.coaching: Safeties split the deep halves. Corners sink, then trigger. Jones and Karlaftis rush four. The rally tackle is the play. Do not open the half by vacating the top of the coverage.

xsandos.title: Zone blitz on second-and-long
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-8 or longer in Atlanta, after a stuffed first-down run
xsandos.why: Spagnuolo’s signature is the call for this down: show heat, drop a lineman, rush a second-level player.
xsandos.coaching: Jones engages and occupies. A linebacker adds from the second level. The dropped lineman walls the hot throw. Bolton fits the run if Atlanta checks out of the pass. Finish the down; the next call is Cover-2 if it becomes third-and-short.

coaching.detail: Reid told the Monday podium that Veach keeps his eyes open, with the cutoff described as Tuesday, November 10, at 3:00 p.m. Arrowhead time. The Atlanta plan should be drawn with the current touch list until a move is announced.
The Jets win was 6-of-11 on third down with Walker, Kelce, Rice, and Worthy taking the targets. That is the script to travel, not a request for more dropbacks after eight quarterback hits.

coaching.topic: Spagnuolo’s standard, not a one-game costume
coaching.detail: Arrowhead Addict framed the Jets day as the pass rush Spagnuolo envisioned, with harder tests ahead. Cover-2 and the zone blitz are the two calls that make that day a rule for Atlanta.

injuries.note: Arrowhead Pride reports Reid labeled three Chiefs day-to-day and names the quarterback. The play-by-play says he was injured on the Q2 sack-fumble Bailey forced and McDonald recovered. He still finished 23-of-31.

personnel.move: Trade-deadline watch, no completed deal in the supplied reports
personnel.detail: Pride’s deadline file and Reid’s comment that Veach keeps his eyes open are the roster story, with receiver smoke noted and the cutoff set for Tuesday, November 10, at 3:00 p.m. Arrowhead time. The Atlanta playmakers stay the players already on the touch list.

strategies: Feature Walker on early-down inside zone and cap the 22-touch spike by mixing Johnson and Ott, who already have touches from the Jets game.
Answer pressure with mesh to Kelce and Rice and a Walker screen before asking for a deep throw to Worthy.
Boot off a real run fake once Atlanta widens, and throw the flat.
Open defensively in Cover-2 and use the zone blitz on second-and-long with Jones occupying.
Protect the red-zone finish that produced five touchdowns, and do not lean on a 51-yard Butker try if the sticks are available.
Keep the third-down standard at or better than 6-of-11 so a 31-minute opponent possession cannot steal a 3.5 game.
debates: Does a 6-2 record with ESPN still at No. 6 deserve more respect, or is FPI’s 78.1 percent in Atlanta the more honest grade?
Should Veach chase a receiver before the Tuesday cutoff, or is Rice-Worthy-Kelce enough after five, six, and four catches?
Is Walker’s 22-touch game the Atlanta plan, or does Buffalo on Thu Nov 26, 7:20 PM CT force a lighter dose?
How much does Mahomes’ day-to-day tag change a 3.5 road lean if he finished 23-of-31?
